description: Reviewed read-only queries over the stock SQLite databases for the DISC gateway data level. Policy as data: the gateway executes only these statements, read-only, with bounded parameters and rows.

system_settings.sql: SELECT LANGUAGE, SYS_THEME, THEME_MODE, LOCK_THEME, FONT_SIZE, BATTERY, POWER_SAVE, VOLUME, MAX_VOL, VOL_MODE, MUTE, EQ_TYPE, FILTER_TYPE, DRE_STATUS, SPDIF, BALANCE_VOL, TREBLE, BASS, PLAY_MODE, MEMORY_PLAY, FOLDER_JUMP, PLAY_GAP, SYS_REPLAY_GAIN, WORK_MODE, INPUT_MODE, USB_MODE, BT_CODEC, BT_STATUS, WIFI_STATUS, NETWORK_MODE, ARTIST_CLASS_TYPE, TRACK_DISPLAY, LIST_OPER_MODE, ONLINE_COVER, ONLINE_LRC, SCREEN_ROT, LIGHT_LEVEL, LIGTH_ON_TIME, OS_MODE, DSD_MODE, DSD_DECODE, OUT_DEV, DEVICE_OUTPUT, CHARGE_PROTECT, AUTO_TIME, KEY_SINGLE_CLICK_SLE, KEY_DOUBLE_CLICK_SLE, KEY_LONG_PRESS_SLE FROM SYSCONFIG WHERE ID = 1

enums.WORK_MODE_INPUT_MODE: see reference remote-modes-themes.md; not a simple index

system_settings.notes: One row of stock settings. LANGUAGE indexes the stock menu order; index 2 (English) confirmed in the emulator, the other positions follow the mq_ui menu table. Live volume/mode/state still come from the protocol; this row is what stock persisted.
system_settings.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db); language order from the mq_ui string table (简体中文, 繁體中文, English, 日本語, 한국어, español, Italiano, Deutsch, français, Русский); reference docs/protocol/remote-settings.md and remote-modes-themes.md for VOL_MODE, FILTER_TYPE, WORK_MODE, INPUT_MODE, BT_CODEC

library_summary.sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SONG) AS tracks, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM MY_LOVE) AS favorites, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM CUSTOM_PLAYLIST_INDEX) AS playlists, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'LIST_SONG_0') AS queue_table, (SELECT MAX(ADD_TIME) FROM SONG) AS last_added, (SELECT MAX(ID) FROM SONG) AS last_id
library_summary.notes: Cheap change detection for client snapshots: compare tracks/last_added/last_id before paging. queue_table says whether stock's queue table exists: stock drops LIST_SONG_0 when a scan removes a queued file and creates it again at the next play, so the counts never read it.
library_summary.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db);

tracks.sql: SELECT ID, PATH, NAME, TITLE, ALBUM, ARTIST, ALBUM_ARTIST, GENRE, DISC, TRACK, DURATION, SAMPLE_RATE, BIT_PER_SAMPLE, CHANNELS, BIT_RATE, SONG_MIMETYPE, SONG_PRODUCTION_YEAR, IS_CUE, IS_ISO, IS_DSD, IS_M3U, M3U_PATH, OFFSET, ADD_TIME FROM SONG ORDER BY ID LIMIT ? OFFSET ?
tracks.notes: Full indexed library with file paths, which protocol catalog pages lack. Positions here are IDs, not stock list positions; selection still needs a fresh protocol read.
tracks.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db);

track_by_id.sql: SELECT ID, PATH, NAME, TITLE, ALBUM, ARTIST, ALBUM_ARTIST, GENRE, DISC, TRACK, DURATION, SAMPLE_RATE, BIT_PER_SAMPLE, CHANNELS, BIT_RATE, SONG_MIMETYPE, SONG_PRODUCTION_YEAR, IS_CUE, IS_ISO, IS_DSD, IS_M3U, M3U_PATH, OFFSET, ADD_TIME FROM SONG WHERE ID = ?
track_by_id.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db);

favorites.sql: SELECT ID, PATH, NAME, TITLE, ALBUM, ARTIST, ALBUM_ARTIST, GENRE, DISC, TRACK, DURATION, SAMPLE_RATE, BIT_PER_SAMPLE, CHANNELS, BIT_RATE, SONG_MIMETYPE, SONG_PRODUCTION_YEAR, IS_CUE, IS_ISO, IS_DSD, IS_M3U, M3U_PATH, OFFSET, ADD_TIME FROM MY_LOVE ORDER BY ID LIMIT ? OFFSET ?
favorites.notes: Built-in favorites with full metadata; ID order is the stock list order.
favorites.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db);

playlists.sql: SELECT ID, LIST_ID, LIST_NAME, M3U_PATH, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM CUSTOM_PLAYLIST p WHERE p.PLAYLIST_ID = i.LIST_ID) AS tracks FROM CUSTOM_PLAYLIST_INDEX i ORDER BY ID
playlists.notes: Custom playlists; the protocol addresses them by position in LIST_ID order, not by ID.
playlists.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db);

playlist_tracks.sql: SELECT PLAYLIST_ID, ID, PATH, NAME, TITLE, ALBUM, ARTIST, ALBUM_ARTIST, GENRE, DISC, TRACK, DURATION, SAMPLE_RATE, BIT_PER_SAMPLE, CHANNELS, BIT_RATE, SONG_MIMETYPE, SONG_PRODUCTION_YEAR, IS_CUE, IS_ISO, IS_DSD, IS_M3U, M3U_PATH, OFFSET, ADD_TIME FROM CUSTOM_PLAYLIST WHERE PLAYLIST_ID = ? ORDER BY ID LIMIT ? OFFSET ?
playlist_tracks.notes: id is CUSTOM_PLAYLIST_INDEX.LIST_ID (the playlists query counts members the same way); the first list has LIST_ID 0.
playlist_tracks.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db);

queue.sql: SELECT ID, LIST_ID, POS_ID, PATH, NAME, TITLE, ALBUM, ARTIST, ALBUM_ARTIST, GENRE, DISC, TRACK, DURATION, IS_CUE, IS_ISO, IS_M3U, M3U_PATH, OFFSET, SONG_TYPE, IS_SELECT FROM LIST_SONG_0 ORDER BY ID
queue.notes: The active queue as stock persisted it; live position comes from the protocol.
queue.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db);

queue_state.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS present FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'LIST_SONG_0'
queue_state.notes: Whether stock has a current queue: LIST_SONG_0 is dropped when a scan removes a queued file and created again at the next play; read this before queue, which fails while the table is gone.
queue_state.evidence: disposable V2.57 guest, 2026-09-29: a scan after deleting a file of the playing album dropped LIST_SONG_0; queue and the old library_summary answered 503 until playback started (owner's player showed the same)

recently_played.sql: SELECT ID, PATH, NAME, TITLE, ALBUM, ARTIST, ALBUM_ARTIST, GENRE, DISC, TRACK, DURATION, PLAY_COUNT, LAST_PLAY_TIME FROM RECORD_SONG ORDER BY LAST_PLAY_TIME DESC LIMIT ?
recently_played.notes: Play history with counts, absent from the protocol.
recently_played.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db);

most_played.sql: SELECT ID, PATH, NAME, TITLE, ALBUM, ARTIST, ALBUM_ARTIST, GENRE, DISC, TRACK, DURATION, PLAY_COUNT, LAST_PLAY_TIME FROM RECORD_SONG ORDER BY PLAY_COUNT DESC, LAST_PLAY_TIME DESC LIMIT ?
most_played.notes: Play history by play count (ties: most recent first), for a "most played" order; rows exist only for tracks stock recorded.
most_played.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db);

resume_point.sql: SELECT MUSIC_ID, IS_PLAYING, POSITION, IS_CUE, IS_ISO, TRACK, IS_NAS, IS_M3U FROM MEMORY_PLAY
resume_point.notes: Stock memory-play record: last track and position in milliseconds.
resume_point.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db);

peq_presets.sql: SELECT ID, STYLE_PRESET, STYLE_NAME, MASTER_GAIN, PARAMS_JSON FROM PEQ ORDER BY ID
peq_presets.notes: STYLE_PRESET is the stored preset enum: user slots 1..10 are 11..20 (network 160..169); rows 160..169 may exist with PARAMS_JSON (null). PARAMS_JSON holds the ten bands with gain and Q as strings.
peq_presets.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db); reference research/docs/reports/peq.md

themes.sql: SELECT ID, POS_ID, NAME, ALIAS, TYPE, USE, IS_SYSTEM, ATTR, SUBCLASS, ALPHA, LOCK_TIME, LOCK_DATE, LOCK_BATTERY, LOCK_ID3, LOCK_MEM_TYPE, FRONT_COLOR, PATH, PREVIEW_PATH FROM CUSTOM_THEME ORDER BY POS_ID
themes.notes: Wallpaper slots; USE marks the active one.
themes.evidence: stock V2.57 schema observed in the disposable guest (/usr/data/fiio/db); reference docs/protocol/remote-modes-themes.md

disliked_tracks.sql: SELECT r.value ->> '$.path' AS path, r.value ->> '$.title' AS title, r.value ->> '$.at' AS disliked_at, (SELECT count(*) FROM plays p WHERE p.path = r.value ->> '$.path') AS plays FROM records r WHERE r.collection = 'disliked' ORDER BY r.value ->> '$.at' DESC, r.id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?
disliked_tracks.notes: Disliked tracks (the store's disliked collection) with their plays in the service's history, newest dislike first.

play_counts.sql: SELECT path, count(*) AS plays, max(started_at) AS last_started_at FROM plays GROUP BY path ORDER BY plays DESC, last_started_at DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?
play_counts.notes: Plays per file over the whole history the service keeps (the route serves only the newest records).
